title: Verifier‑Guided Generate→Validate→Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration: A Confirmatory Study
abstract: We evaluate whether adding a deterministic network verifier to an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals. Under a preregistered paired design (CNSM2026-A1-prereg-v1; preregistration SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) we synthesized 200 stratified intent→configuration tasks and ran paired episodes with gpt-5-mini under two conditions: baseline (LLM‑alone) and guarded (LLM + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + one automated repair iteration). On 188 complete pairs (376 completed episodes; 24 failed episodes) the guarded vs baseline success rates were 1.000 and 0.9840425531914894, respectively; paired difference = 0.015957446808510634, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0, 0.03723404255319149], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute change ≥0.20) was not observed. We add an explicit repair‑activity summary (repair invocations = 3; these correspond to the three discordant guarded‑only successes, n_10 = 3) and document where per‑episode provider traces and the full execution manifest are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7; execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865). We reconcile a preregistration wording inconsistency (regression‑rate vs success‑rate) by reporting the executed estimand (paired success‑rate difference) and release the full artifact bundle for reproducibility.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed for intent→configuration translation in network operations (NetOps). Operational adoption requires reliable, auditable behavior: proposals must avoid functional regressions and unsafe intermediate states. A common safety architecture is generate→validate→repair: an LLM proposes a configuration, a deterministic verifier checks functional invariants, and, if violations are found, an automated repair step attempts to fix the proposal. Despite architectural interest, preregistered quantitative evidence isolating verifier impact in a within‑task paired design is limited. We therefore ask: Does integrating a deterministic verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce functional regressions and blast radius versus an LLM‑alone pipeline on a seeded synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired confirmatory design (CNSM2026-A1-prereg-v1; prereg SHA256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3); (2) a Dockerized execution/analysis pipeline (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) exercising gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 across 200 stratified tasks with full archival of prompts, outputs, and verifier traces; (3) a transparent, artifact‑backed confirmatory analysis showing a small, inconclusive guarded benefit and a concise repair‑activity summary drawn from archived execution artifacts.
sections.related_work: Prior work spans intent‑to‑config translation, LLM‑based program/recipe repair, and verifier/guardrail architectures. Recent Cornetto‑style benchmarks and LLM→IaC studies evaluate translation accuracy; CRITIC‑style and verifier‑augmented agent work demonstrate tool‑interactive self‑correction. MeshAgent and other NetOps frameworks describe translation+verification pipelines, but few studies provide preregistered paired inference isolating verifier effect with full artifact release. We position this study as a preregistered, within‑task paired evaluation focusing on operationally meaningful functional correctness and blast‑radius metrics rather than broad model ranking.
sections.methodology: Preregistration & estimand: The preregistered plan CNSM2026-A1-prereg-v1 (SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) specified a paired design with primary estimand = paired success‑rate difference P(success|guarded) − P(success|baseline). (The preregistration also used regression‑rate phrasing; regression_rate_difference = − success_rate_difference. We report the executed estimand and provide numeric equivalence to the preregistered wording.) Task generation: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 produced 200 stratified intent→golden‑config tasks constrained to verifier‑supported feature sets (planned topology strata: small/medium/large; vendor‑mix constraints). Execution: adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1 executed paired episodes using gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd). Guarded behavior: for each shared initial candidate the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 validated proposals and, upon violation, a single automated repair attempt was allowed (one repair call maximum; preregistered). Logging & archiving: all prompts, raw model outputs, validator traces, parsed IRs, seeds, and provider call traces were archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7; execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865). Analysis: primary test = exact McNemar paired test on complete pairs, with 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) for the paired difference; missingness policy 'complete_pair_primary' was applied (exclude pairs where both episodes failed) with a preregistered sensitivity treating failures as regressions.
sections.results: Execution accounting: planned episodes = 400; completed = 376; failed = 24 (both_missing_pairs = 12 pairs excluded from primary analysis); complete_pairs included = 188. Primary contingency (complete pairs): n_11 = 185 (both success), n_10 = 3 (guarded success only), n_01 = 0 (baseline success only), n_00 = 0 (both failure). Source artifacts: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766) and analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = b1a44ab88b072eb28328261a9a0e0eba39820a3b0d11e5dd6e688e3d7ca045b7). Primary estimates (complete‑pair analysis): baseline_successes = 185/188 = 0.9840425531914894; guarded_successes = 188/188 = 1.0; paired difference = 0.015957446808510634. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 reps, seed=1729) for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.03723404255319149]. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute change ≥ 0.20) was not met. Missingness & sensitivity: treating the 12 both‑missing pairs as regressions (prespecified sensitivity) yields the same discordant counts (n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0) and paired difference = 3/200 = 0.015; McNemar p remains 0.25. Repair activity and reconciliation: provider call audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json) logs 'repair' stage invoked 3 times (stage_counts.repair = 3) and the guarded condition invoked in three guarded‑only episodes; these three repair‑stage invocations correspond exactly to the three discordant pairs (n_10 = 3) that changed from baseline failure to guarded success. Concise repair‑activity summary (artifact‑grounded): Table 1 (below) reports the aggregate repair activity available in archived artifacts; per‑episode provider traces and the full per‑call manifest (with exact episode/pair IDs and call traces) are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) and can be inspected for the explicit episode IDs.
sections.discussion: The observed point estimate modestly favors the guarded pipeline (~1.6 pp) but is far below the preregistered 20‑pp efficacy threshold and is not statistically significant. Two operational explanations are evident from the archived artifacts: (1) ceiling effect — baseline correctness was high (≈98.4%), leaving little absolute headroom for verifier improvements; (2) verifier coverage and task selection — the deterministic verifier supports a limited feature set and, for this synthetic task family, most LLM proposals already satisfied oracle constraints or matched golden configs, so repairs were rarely invoked (repair invocations = 3). The small number of discordant pairs (3) drives low realized power despite the prespecified sample size. Implications: verifier‑guided pipelines provide auditability and can correct some failures (here, 3 guarded‑only successes), but measurable benefits depend on baseline error rates, verifier feature coverage, and task difficulty. Future work should test task families with higher baseline error and broader verifier scope, multiple models, and iterative repair budgets to better quantify blast‑radius reduction.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation (200 planned tasks) of an LLM (gpt‑5‑mini) with and without a deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on a Cornetto‑like synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark, the guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline yielded a small, inconclusive improvement in success rate (paired difference ≈ 0.016; 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.037234]; exact McNemar p = 0.25). The preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target was not reached. Artifact evidence indicates few repair interventions (3) because baseline LLM proposals were highly correct for this task family and verifier coverage was constrained. We publish the preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, provider traces, and analysis artifacts to enable reproducible follow‑up studies that vary baseline difficulty, verifier scope, and model ensembles.

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt‑5‑mini): results do not imply generality across models or model families.
Synthetic Cornetto‑like benchmark: task realism and production telemetry are limited; external validity to operational networks is constrained.
High baseline correctness (≈98.4%) produced a ceiling effect that reduced observable verifier impact in this task family.
Verifier scope limited to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 supported features; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded from confirmatory analysis.
Completed pairs fewer than planned (188 of 200) due to 24 failed episodes; missingness handled per preregistered policy (complete_pair_primary).
Repair‑stage invocations were rare in this run (repair stage logged = 3), limiting conclusions about iterative repair dynamics and blast‑radius effects.

Required revisions unresolved due to absent explicit fields in supplied artifacts: (a) per‑episode repair provider‑call IDs for the three repair invocations are archived in the full execution/provider_calls/ and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7); the present manuscript reports their aggregate effect (n_10 = 3) and points to the archived traces for explicit IDs; (b) the preregistered stratified outcome breakdown by explicit topology‑scale (small/medium/large) and vendor‑mix strata could not be included here because the supplied analysis artifacts did not include a labeled, finalized stratified summary table; the task_manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865) contains per‑task metadata that enables computing these strata breakdowns offline from the archive, and we point readers to that manifest for reproducible subgroup computations.
